items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I decided to change teachers, because I had heard of this wonderful teacher, Arthur Reeves. I went to him, and he took me on, and I certainly got much out of him that kind of structured what I do and how I sound today.

ctx.x: Let’s see. Did we mention . . . we didn’t mention Arthur Reeves at all?

Oh, well, that’s . . . oh, I couldn’t go on without mentioning Arthur Reeves, because after a bit I decided to change teachers, because I had heard of this wonderful teacher, Arthur Reeves. I went to him, and he took me on, and I certainly got much out of him that kind of structured what I do and how I sound today. He was a fine teacher. He was a fine entertainer, as you had to be in those days unless you were what they called a hot jazz player, you know. He did parties and weddings and all of that, and dances.…

At some point you also discovered some books, I understand, that you’ve used to . . . I believe, told us in the past that you found some, you know, saxophone method books or music theory books or something, whatever you could get your hand on, and you did some studying of your own, just on [unclear].

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Of course, after Lieutenant Michael, I studied with a man named Arthur Reeves, who really hit -- his emphasis was on sound.

ctx.x: And then I went to a teacher named Michael -- what was his first name? Eugene. Yes. And I studied with him for a while; he also had 2 sons who were fine musicians -- Otto and Gene Jr. After studying with him a while, he turned me over -- well, at the beginning, he turned me over to who was his star pupil, Rudy Powell, who was a very fine musician. Rudy had also played violin.

Then after I studied with Michael a while -- I don't remember how long -- I went to a teacher named Arthur Reeves, with whom I studied for, oh, maybe a year or more -- and he was a very, very fine saxophone player. I tried to develop the sound that he was getting because the sound that he got was great.
Excuse me. What kind of playing did he do? Was he a performing musician or was he ...
